generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential unique integers starting at 1; never NULL; no duplicates.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy from the parent key pool (extended to include any boundary literals required for the child column); allow parent rows without children; no NULL unless the column is nullable; keep referential integrity; for composite-PK child tables, draw the non-grouping FK from a pool that excludes values already paired with the chosen grouping key so the composite PK stays unique.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Uniform choice from the column's enum list; occasionally emit a case variant (lower/upper) for LIKE near-variants.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Random short token from a fixed pool of 5-12 distinct values.
generic_sampling_rules.nullable: For each nullable column, ~5% of rows get NULL; at least one NULL row per instance; never plant NULL on NOT NULL / PK / FK columns; plant NULLs before group/ties/boundary planting so required structure is not erased.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary: For numeric columns with listed literals, include the literal, literal-1 and literal+1; for FK child columns, extend the parent pool so the literals exist and inject them into the child.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates: For DISTINCT-target columns, ensure 20-50% duplicate share; applies to FK child columns too.
generic_sampling_rules.ties: For ORDER/LIMIT-target columns, plant ties at the listed ranks in both ASC and DESC directions on the aggregated group counts of the actual grouping column (taughtBy.p_id, taughtBy.course_id); apply after the group structure is fixed and PK-deduped; verify by querying the written instance.
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: Ensure groups of size 1, 2 and >=3 exist for GROUP BY-target columns; applies to FK child columns too.
generic_sampling_rules.aggregate_boundary: For aggregate-target columns, construct groups straddling the listed HAVING thresholds (e.g. sizes 3 and 5 for COUNT(*), 4 and 5 for COUNT(col)) while preserving FK integrity; make the aggregate-group builder PK-aware so the non-grouping FK is drawn from a pool excluding already-used (grouping_key, other_fk) pairs; compute group counts on the final deduplicated row set and verify post-write that COUNT(*) and COUNT(DISTINCT taughtby.course_id) straddle the thresholds.

semantic_rules_and_formulas.evidence: added semantic constraint: no self-advising; not implied by schema

supporting_evidence.course.courseLevel: Observed values Level_500, Level_300, Level_400; distinct=3.
supporting_evidence.person.professor: Observed values 0,1; distinct=2. Domain is exactly {0,1}; boundary literals -1/2 are comparison probes only and are never emitted as non-NULL values.
supporting_evidence.person.student: Observed values 1,0; distinct=2. Domain is exactly {0,1}; boundary literals -1/2 are comparison probes only and are never emitted as non-NULL values.
supporting_evidence.person.hasPosition: Observed values 0, Faculty, Faculty_adj, Faculty_eme, Faculty_aff; distinct=5.
supporting_evidence.person.inPhase: Observed values 0, Post_Quals, Post_Generals, Pre_Quals; distinct=4.
supporting_evidence.person.yearsInProgram: Observed values 0, Year_2, Year_5, Year_7, Year_10, Year_3, Year_1, Year_6; statistics report distinct=12, so the domain is extended to 12 values: the 8 observed plus Year_4, Year_8, Year_9, Year_11; case variants year_1/year_2 are boundary probes only.
supporting_evidence.advisedBy composite FK: Schema declares foreign key (p_id, p_id_dummy) references person(p_id, p_id); since person.p_id is the PK, the tuple (p_id, p_id) is unique and the composite FK is satisfiable by drawing both child columns from person.p_id. The p_id <> p_id_dummy rule is an added semantic constraint (no self-advising), not implied by the schema.

uncertainty: advisedBy FK references person(p_id,p_id) which is not a declared unique tuple in person; treated as two independent FKs to person.p_id for generation (p_id and p_id_dummy each drawn from person.p_id, p_id <> p_id_dummy to avoid self-advising). This guarantees the composite tuple exists because person.p_id is unique. Nullable columns have null_rate 0.0 in stats but are declared nullable; NULLs are still planted per instruction 10. yearsInProgram distinct=12 in stats vs 8 observed values; domain extended to 12 values (Year_4, Year_8, Year_9, Year_11 added) with case variants as boundary probes only. person.inPhase is TEXT; numeric boundary targets [-1,0,1] from the atomic summary are dropped as contradictory with the TEXT enum domain, keeping only the TEXT enum plus '0'. person.professor/student boundary literals -1/2 are kept as sampling-domain boundary probes but the semantic rule restricts non-NULL values to IN (0,1); boundary probes outside the domain are not emitted as non-NULL values. taughtBy aggregate-group builder must be PK-aware to avoid duplicate (course_id, p_id) tuples; ties and aggregate thresholds must be verified on the written instance after dedup.
